gallery.filename: Çinili Köşk Museum Ceramic plate. Height- 7 cm, Diameter- 45½ cm. From Iznik, c. 1500. Inv. n0 41 9 in 2018 01 523.jpg
gallery.title: File:Çinili Köşk Museum Ceramic plate. Height- 7 cm, Diameter- 45½ cm. From Iznik, c. 1500. Inv. n0 41 9 in 2018 01 523.jpg
gallery.source: Çinili Köşk Museum Ceramic plate. Height- 7 cm, Diameter- 45½ cm. From Iznik, c. 1500. Inv. n0 41 9 in 2018 01 523
gallery.description:
Ceramic plate. Height: 7 cm, Diameter: 45½ cm. From Iznik, c. 1500. Inv. n0 41/9. The colour on the next picture is closer to the original.
An example of the pure white ground on which the cobalt blue design (large rumis and cloud bands, scrolling branches and blossoms) is depicted. These designs were drawn by the artists of the Topkapı Sarayı workshop and sent to the potters at Iznik for transfer to the tile panels and plates, which were not only used in the mosques and palaces of the Ottoman Empire, but were exported all over Europe.

gallery.filename: Çinili Köşk Museum Mosque lamp from the Beyazit II Mausoleum in 2018 03 529.jpg
gallery.title: File:Çinili Köşk Museum Mosque lamp from the Beyazit II Mausoleum in 2018 03 529.jpg
gallery.source: Çinili Köşk Museum Mosque lamp from the Beyazit II Mausoleum in 2018 03 529
gallery.description:
From circa 1512. As it is from Bayezids tomb it can be dated pretty precisely. It is similar to work from the “Master of the Knots” but here another master uses large lotus leaves and rosettes. 
Sorry for colour changes in later pictures.

gallery.source: Istanbul Çinili Köşk Porch in 2018 04 6257
gallery.description: One of pictures taken at the porch of the museum, with a fine iwan with blue and white tiled decoration. The present portico consisting of 14 marble columns was constructed during the reign of Abdülhamid I (1774-1789) after the (original) old wooden portico burned down in 1737.
